headline.headline: BRUNSON DRAGS KNICKS PAST CAVS IN OVERTIME THRILLER
headline.deck: New York outlasts Cleveland 115-104 in OT to seize Game 1 edge
headline.body:
NEW YORK — Jalen Brunson delivered when the Knicks needed him most, refusing to let New York surrender a golden home-court opportunity as the Knicks defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 115-104 in overtime Tuesday night in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals. The victory gives New York a 1-0 series lead heading into Game 2, a commanding early position for a franchise that has chased a championship for decades.

The Cavaliers, the fourth seed out of the East at 52-30, entered Madison Square Garden as a dangerous opponent, but Brunson and the Knicks, who finished 53-29, exploited Cleveland's defensive scheme late to force the extra period and then pull away. The overtime session proved decisive, as New York's superior ball movement and defensive intensity wore down a Cavaliers squad that could not find consistent answers.

Game 2 goes Wednesday night in New York, where the Knicks will look to extend their advantage before the series shifts to Cleveland. For a franchise starved of deep playoff runs, the overtime win carries weight beyond a single game.

secondary.headline: BRAVES ERUPT FOR THREE IN EIGHTH, BURY MARLINS 8-4
secondary.deck: Atlanta's big eighth inning breaks the game open in Miami
secondary.body:
MIAMI — The Atlanta Braves turned a manageable lead into a rout Tuesday, scoring three runs in the eighth inning to put away the Miami Marlins 8-4 before 7,521 fans at loanDepot park. Faucher earned the win on the mound as Atlanta improved its position in the NL East standings with a performance that was businesslike through seven before turning decisive in the eighth.

Austin Riley was hit by a pitch from Bachar at some point in the contest, adding an edge to a game that Atlanta controlled on the scoreboard. The Braves scored in five different innings, tacking on a run in the fifth, sixth, eighth and ninth to gradually pull away. Miami managed four runs but could never sustain a threat capable of matching Atlanta's steady accumulation.

secondary.headline: HURRICANES AND CANADIENS OPEN THIRD ROUND WITH FRESH STAKES
secondary.deck: Carolina and Montreal square off as the conference finals begin
secondary.body:
The NHL's second round has given way to the conference finals, and the matchup between the Carolina Hurricanes and the Montreal Canadiens represents one of the sport's more compelling regional contrasts. Carolina, which finished 53-22-7 in the Metropolitan Division, brings a depth-driven, defensively disciplined identity into the series, while Montreal, 48-24-10 in the Atlantic, carries the energy of a resurgent franchise that has already dispatched two playoff opponents.

Out west, the Vegas Golden Knights and Colorado Avalanche meet in the Western Conference Finals, a series carrying its own intrigue after word circulated that Cale Makar's status has clouded Colorado's outlook. The Avalanche without Makar at full strength represent a significantly different challenge, and Vegas will look to exploit any gaps as the series opens.

secondary.headline: FLORES LAWYERS SERVE SUBPOENAS TO 25 NFL TEAMS IN DISCRIMINATION SUIT
secondary.deck: Court filings reveal widening scope of Brian Flores' legal battle against league
secondary.body:
The legal battle between former NFL head coach Brian Flores and the league expanded significantly this week after court filings revealed that Flores' attorneys have served subpoenas to 25 NFL teams. The development signals that Flores' discrimination lawsuit, originally filed against the NFL and several franchises, has broadened into a sweeping examination of hiring practices across the league.

Commissioner Roger Goodell said Tuesday that the NFL is cooperating with Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier after the league received a separate subpoena from that office, adding another layer of legal scrutiny to the organization. Separately, sources confirmed that Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice underwent cleanup surgery on his right knee last week, though the full implications for Rice's availability heading into the 2026 season remain unclear.

column.headline: THE KNICKS ARE FOR REAL, AND THE GARDEN KNOWS IT
column.body:
There is a difference between a team that wins a playoff game and a team that knows how to win a playoff game. Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden, the Knicks looked very much like the latter. Overtime against the Cavaliers is not a gift or a fluke. It is a stress test, and New York passed it. Brunson has spent years being told his team is not quite good enough, that the window is narrow, that Cleveland or Boston or Milwaukee will eventually close the door. Game 1 was his answer.

The Eastern Conference Finals is a long road and the Cavaliers, who won 52 games this season, will not fold quietly. But the Knicks now hold serve on their home floor and carry genuine momentum into Game 2. For a city that last celebrated a championship in 1973, that is not nothing. It is, in fact, the closest thing to a promise this franchise has offered its fans in a very long time.

story.headline: NATIONALS BATTER METS IN HIGH-SCORING SLUGFEST, WOOD'S BAT LEADS WASHINGTON TO 9-6 WIN
story.deck: James Wood's 13th homer powers Nationals past slumping Mets in wild affair
story.body:
WASHINGTON — The Nationals wasted no time Tuesday night, erupting for three runs in the first inning and never looking back, beating the New York Mets 9-6 at Nationals Park in a game that featured four home runs, three hit batters, and a 46-minute delay. James Wood crushed his 13th homer of the season, pacing a Washington offense that finished with nine runs on a night when both benches were emptied after multiple hit batsmen rattled the proceedings.

The Mets tried to answer, pushing across four runs in the second inning to knot the game at five before Washington responded with two more in the top half of that same frame to retake control. Bo Bichette went deep for his fifth homer of the year, and Juan Soto added his seventh for New York, but the Mets could not sustain any of their rallies. Jose Tena also connected for Washington, his third of the season, giving the Nationals four long balls on the night. Pitchers Griffin and McLean combined to hit three Washington batters, including CJ Abrams and prospect Millas, inflaming tensions throughout the contest.

The loss dropped New York to 21-27, fifth in the NL East, while Washington climbed to 24-25 with its third win in the series. The two clubs meet again Wednesday night at Nationals Park, with the Mets desperate to avoid falling further behind in the division standings. Attendance was 22,754.

story.headline: BRUNSON BURNS HARDEN AS KNICKS STEAL GAME 1 FROM CAVALIERS, 115-104
story.deck: Jalen Brunson torches Cleveland in fourth-quarter surge to give New York the series edge.
story.body:
NEW YORK — Jalen Brunson turned James Harden into a footnote Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden, orchestrating a stunning second-half rally that lifted the New York Knicks past the Cleveland Cavaliers, 115-104, in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals. Brunson, cool and relentless in the fourth quarter, dissected Cleveland's defense with pull-up jumpers and driving layups while Harden struggled to contain the Knicks' star guard at the other end, surrendering drives and failing to match Brunson's killer instincts in the game's most critical moments.

Cleveland led for stretches of the first half and appeared poised to control the tempo, but the Cavaliers unraveled down the stretch as Brunson imposed his will. Coach Kenny Atkinson drew criticism for holding his timeouts during the Cavs' fourth-quarter collapse, watching helplessly from the sideline as New York went on a decisive run that erased Cleveland's lead and silenced whatever optimism the road contingent had carried into the Garden.

The Knicks, seeded third in the East at 53-29, now hold a 1-0 series advantage over the fourth-seeded Cavaliers, who finished 52-30. Game 2 tips off Thursday, with Cleveland desperate to correct its late-game breakdowns before returning to Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse, where the series could quickly tilt further in New York's favor if Brunson and the Knicks carry this momentum north.

story.headline: MAKAR MYSTERY CLOUDS AVALANCHE AS WCF OPENS AGAINST GOLDEN KNIGHTS
story.deck: Colorado's star defenseman misses practice again, raising alarms ahead of Game 1
story.body:
DENVER -- Cale Makar, the cornerstone of the Colorado Avalanche blue line and one of the most dangerous offensive defensemen in the game, sat out practice Tuesday for the second consecutive session on the eve of Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals against the Vegas Golden Knights. The Avalanche offered no timetable for his return and listed him as day-to-day, leaving head coach Jared Bednar with a gaping question mark at the most critical juncture of Colorado's postseason run. Without Makar quarterbacking the power play and logging his customary 25-plus minutes, the Avalanche look considerably more vulnerable against a Vegas club that went 53-22-7 in the regular season.

The Golden Knights, meanwhile, are navigating their own off-ice turbulence. Multiple NHL franchises remain in a holding pattern waiting for permission to interview former Vegas coach Bruce Cassidy, whom the organization has yet to allow to speak with other teams despite his departure. That front-office distraction has done nothing to slow a Vegas roster loaded with Nathan MacKinnon's former nemesis, Jack Eichel, and a defense corps that suffocated opponents all spring. Analyst Greg Wyshynski identified goaltending depth, special teams efficiency, and Colorado's ability to replace Makar's production as the three pivotal factors when the puck drops Wednesday night.

Elsewhere around the league, the Eastern Conference Finals picture sharpened Tuesday as the Montreal Canadiens and Carolina Hurricanes officially opened their third-round series. Montreal, which finished 48-24-10 in the Atlantic Division, enters as the underdog against a Carolina team that posted a 53-22-7 record in the rugged Metropolitan Division and has steamrolled opponents with suffocating defensive structure all playoffs. In New Jersey, the Devils brought stability to their own situation by confirming that Sheldon Keefe will return behind the bench next season after new general manager Sunny Mehta completed his review of the coaching staff, giving the franchise a clear direction heading into the offseason.

story.headline: RECEIVER MARKET EXPLODES AS TEAMS SCRAMBLE TO UPGRADE PASSING GAMES THIS SPRING
story.deck: Top wideouts command record contracts as franchises retool rosters ahead of training camp.
story.body:
The wide receiver market shattered expectations this May, with Davante Adams landing a two-year, $62 million deal with the Dallas Cowboys after the Raiders declined his option, giving quarterback Dak Prescott a proven target to anchor a retooled offense heading into 2026. The move sent ripples across the league, pushing the market value for veteran pass-catchers to historic levels just weeks after the draft added a fresh wave of talent to the mix.

The Cleveland Browns made the boldest draft investment at the position, selecting speedy Tennessee wideout Cam Whitfield with the fifth overall pick, betting the 21-year-old's elite route-running and 4.33 speed can jump-start an offense that ranked 28th in passing yards during the 2025 season. General manager Andrew Berry called Whitfield the most complete receiver prospect since Justin Jefferson entered the league, drawing both admiration and skepticism from scouts around the NFL.

Meanwhile, the Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers quietly emerged as players in the veteran trade market, with Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst in active discussions to acquire Tampa Bay Buccaneers slot receiver Chris Godwin before training camps open in late July. League sources say Godwin, recovering from a late-season ankle injury, is eager for a fresh start, and Green Bay views the 30-year-old as the missing piece to push Jordan Love back into championship contention.
